newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet fuel firms while gas oil softens.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet fuel firms while gas oil softens.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on Wednesday with jet fuel edging up on renewed buying from North Asia for the winter amid tight regional supplies, traders said.
"There is some buying interest seen from Japan and South Korea for January cargoes," one trader said. Both countries have recently raised their jet/kerosene purchases for the winter.

As a result premiums have increased by about 50 cents to over $2.00 per barrel to spot Singapore prices on a cost-and-freight basis. The January jet/gas oil spread traded at $1.30 a barrel, up 10 cents from Tuesday.
On the physical market a major was offering 240,000 barrels of jet fuel for lifting on January 8-12 at $33.55 per barrel.
Gas oil prices eased slightly despite expectations of renewed buying from China for late January arrival cargoes.

China had bought more than one million tonnes for arrival in December and most traders were of the opinion that it had covered its requirements in the run up to the Lunar New Year holiday in early February.
A trader was offering 150,000 barrels of gas oil at $32.70 a barrel against a bid at $32.40 both for Jan 8-12 lifting fob, down from Tuesday's traded level of $32.95.
Gasoline was unchanged in a quiet market with a major heard seeking a small lot of 92-octane unleaded for first-half January lifting but no firm level was indicated.
A European major confirmed the Taiwan reformate award at $25.75 a barrel for February 11-20 but the Dutch trader's January 18-27 award was not confirmed at $26.20.
Naphtha was steady with January swap bid at $24.00 per barrel. But physical was quiet and no change seen in the naphtha/crude spread at $64 per tonne, traders said.
Fuel oil firmed on buying from a local trader who bought a 20,000-tonne at $124.00 per tonne from a European major.
